prompt.en: A replacement fuse has the specified current rating, but its voltage rating is lower than the equipment manual requires. What is the safety problem?

text.en: The fuse may not interrupt the circuit safely and could sustain an arc
The fuse will necessarily open during normal receive current
The fuse will lower the equipment's normal supply voltage
The fuse will act as a surge suppressor for lightning transients

explanation.en: A fuse needs both the correct current rating and a voltage rating high enough to interrupt the fault without maintaining an arc.

prompt.en: An indoor antenna test is moved from 1 m away from a marked keep-clear line to 2 m away in the same direction, with the same power and antenna. In the simple free-space model, what happens to power density at that line?

text.en: It falls to about one quarter
It falls to about one half
It stays the same because frequency did not change
It increases because the antenna is farther from the operator

explanation.en: Power density follows the inverse-square relationship in the simple free-space model, so doubling distance reduces it to roughly 1/4.

prompt.en: You plan to use an indoor transmitting antenna during a short low-power test. Which setup gives the best RF-safety margin?

text.en: Place it beside the operating chair to shorten the coax
Aim a high-gain beam through an occupied room
Hang it where people can brush against the feed point
Keep it as far as practical from occupied spaces and control access

explanation.en: Distance and access control are conservative RF-safety tools, especially for indoor antennas.
